story:
The Remnants keep a post on the south-west of Modernagrav, with a griffon and a stablemaster, because the dwarves would rather watch the dig than be surprised by it. The post has a watch. Alivor and Asutri keep it, and they keep it against everyone.

The dwarves' oldest slates call the island beyond the rockwall by a word that means the place one does not dig, and the clans that crossed to Aegir in the first boats agreed among themselves that nobody would. The morvalt broke that agreement with picks and fire. The Remnants could not stop them, but they could keep the agreement themselves, and they decided at the slate-house, the dwarves say, that the post on Modernagrav would let nobody pass toward the bones who had not earned the dwarves' trust: no morvalt, no sjoalf, no Vendo, and no stranger of Midgard either, whose explorers had come through the gap with the dwarves' own and wanted, the dwarves thought, to dig.

Alivor is the elder of the watch, a tracker by training, who walked the island with Orri of Hagall in the first season and saw what the morvalt found. He came back from it with a single opinion that he has repeated to every traveller since, usually with an axe in his hand: that the bones are not the Mother and are not a cow and are not anything the dwarves have a word for, and that the right number of people digging at them is none. He does not ask whose side a stranger is on. A stranger who has not proved a friend to the Remnants, by the dwarves' long reckoning of deeds, is a stranger walking toward the bones.

His watch is his clan. The dwarves of the post come when he is struck, as the Remnants have always come for each other, and the slate-house keeps account of everyone who strikes one of them. The griffon at the post flies only friends. Alivor says that is the whole of the dwarves' law in one sentence, and that Midgard would do well to remember it.
legend: Alivor is a level 50 iarn dwarf of the Remnants near their post in south-western Modernagrav. He's Remnants faction and AGGRESSIVE: if your standing with the Remnants is low, he attacks you on sight, and the dwarves next to him (an iarn dwarf and a tracker) come too via bring-a-friend. No special abilities, not CC-immune. Think before you kill him: killing faction members shifts your faction standing the usual way, and the Remnants run the griffon post here and in Faraheim. If you're raising Remnants faction, go around; if you don't care, he and Asutri are an easy pair for a group of 50s. Hermione the stablemaster is close by and isn't hostile.

loremasterTopic.text: Elder of the Remnants' watch at the [post], a tracker who walked the island with [Orri]. He holds that the right number of people digging at the [bones] is none, and attacks those the dwarves do not trust.

bookPage: From the slates of Orri of Hagall: Alivor walked with me the first season. He is a better tracker than I am a slate-writer, and he read the ground round the bones for a day and then sat down and would not go nearer. I asked him what he had read. He said the beasts of the vigil had all come there walking, from every side of the island, a long time ago, and none of them had ever walked away. He said a dwarf does not need a slate to know what that means. I wrote it down anyway.
